subsystems.name: Chiral building blocks
subsystems.role: supply the mirror-image monomers that natural biology never uses.

subsystems.name: Mirror biopolymers
subsystems.role: link those monomers into mirror proteins and mirror DNA or RNA.

subsystems.name: Mirror translation machinery
subsystems.role: would let a mirror cell build its own mirror proteins instead of relying on chemists.

subsystems.name: Mirror cell chassis
subsystems.role: the compartment, membrane and metabolism that would make it a living cell.

subsystems.name: Detection toolkit
subsystems.role: how you would tell a mirror organism from ordinary life once it exists.
parts: growth tests that fail with natural nutrients

subsystems.name: Risk modelling and screening
subsystems.role: estimates whether a mirrored organism could survive and spread, and intercepts attempts to build one.

buildSteps.title: Make the mirror monomers
buildSteps.detail: D-amino acids are produced by chemical synthesis or by resolving a racemic mixture, and L-sugars are made from L-ribose. Enantiopurity matters: a trace of the natural handedness can feed ordinary microbes.

buildSteps.title: Assemble mirror proteins chemically
buildSteps.detail: Solid-phase synthesis can build chains tens of residues long; ligation joins fragments to reach a few hundred. The largest mirror enzymes made this way so far are roughly the size of a small polymerase.

buildSteps.title: Make mirror nucleic acids
buildSteps.detail: L-nucleotides are joined into mirror DNA and RNA, either chemically or with a mirror polymerase built from D-amino acids. Mirror genes can be copied without any natural enzyme present.

buildSteps.title: Rebuild translation
buildSteps.detail: The hard step: a mirror ribosome with thousands of amino acids and thousands of RNA bases, plus mirror tRNAs and synthetases. No one has come close; it would have to be assembled and folded without natural chaperones.

buildSteps.title: Close a mirror metabolism
buildSteps.detail: Every enzyme in the energy, cofactor and membrane pathways would need mirror counterparts, and chiral cofactors such as mirror ATP would have to be supplied or made.

buildSteps.title: Wrap it in a mirror membrane
buildSteps.detail: Mirror lipids are synthesised and assembled into a vesicle, then a mirror genome of several hundred genes is introduced. This is the point at which a self-replicating mirror cell would exist.

buildSteps.title: Test what could stop it
buildSteps.detail: The mirror organism is grown with natural microbes, phages, grazing protists and immune cells to measure whether anything can eat, infect or clear it.

buildSteps.title: Screen, detect and decide
buildSteps.detail: Order-screening flags purchases of mirror building blocks and mirror-life genes; chiral analysis watches for mirror molecules in waste and environmental samples. Regulators decide whether any construction is permitted at all.

prerequisites.why: bulk D-amino acids and L-sugars are needed before any mirror polymer can be attempted.
mirror enzymes have been made in small amounts, but not the large, multi-subunit machinery a cell needs.
without a working mirror ribosome, a mirror organism cannot build its own parts.
chiral chromatography and circular dichroism work in the lab but are not deployed for environmental surveillance.
the technology is pre-emptive: the decision not to build it is the main safeguard, and it needs international agreement.

pathway.milestone: a 2024 technical report in Science concluded mirror bacteria are not yet constructible and called for a moratorium plus more biosafety research
pathway.unlocks: a shared technical baseline and a window to build detection before capability arrives.

pathway.milestone: cheaper mirror monomers, longer mirror proteins and routine chiral detection methods
pathway.unlocks: the ability to notice mirror synthesis and to study mirror molecules safely.

pathway.milestone: mirror gene replication and translation working in a test tube without cells
pathway.unlocks: a clear signal that a mirror cell is technically within reach, and a decision point.

pathway.milestone: either a contained mirror cell under strict physical isolation, or a durable international prohibition
pathway.unlocks: if built: a new field of synthetic biology that nature cannot eat, infect or reliably clear.
